findings_addressed: LEG 4 (TC-76 / sqlite-vec #99) — probe REPRODUCES and is live in FathomDB. sqlite-vec =0.1.7 `vec0Update_Delete_ClearMetadata` (sqlite-vec.c:8888) deletes the `_metadatatext<NN>` shadow row for a TEXT metadata value longer than the 12-byte inline view and then returns `sqlite3_step`'s SQLITE_DONE (101) verbatim, never resetting `rc` to SQLITE_OK; `vec0Update_Delete` (sqlite-vec.c:9027) reads 101 as an error and aborts the whole DELETE. The INSERT/UPDATE twin (sqlite-vec.c:8258-8320) is rescued by an unconditional `rc = sqlite3_blob_close(...)` after its switch, so only DELETE carries the defect.

LEG 4 — measured boundaries. Bare vec0: value bytes 1/11/12 delete Ok; 13/64/1024 fail with extended_code 101 and leave the row. Real engine via `erase_source`: raw attribute value 10 bytes -> stored 11 -> Ok; raw 11 -> stored 12 -> Ok; raw 12 -> stored 13 -> Err(Storage), row left; raw 13 -> stored 14 -> Err(Storage). The +1 shift is Slice 15e's `\x01 || V` present-marker encoding. `purge` fails identically.

LEG 4 — reachability. `kind` CANNOT exceed 12 bytes in vector_default: every enrolment door (Engine::vector_kind_needs_enrolment lib.rs:4920, enqueue_declared_vector_backfill lib.rs:17538) and the commit itself gate on `kind_is_vector_committable` -> `resolve_source_type`, max 9 bytes. `source_type` is a vec0 PARTITION KEY (different storage, #99 does not apply) with the same <=9-byte domain. `status` ships the '' sentinel. The attr COLUMN-NAME axis is a RED HERRING and this is now stated explicitly: `attr_vec0_column` renders `attr_ + hex(name)`, so any attribute name of >=4 chars already yields a >12-char identifier (e.g. `priority` -> `attr_7072696f72697479`, 20 chars) and the shipped Slice-15e corpus exercises that today. attr VALUES are the sole exposure.

LEG 4 — remediation. `delete_vector_partition_row` + `neutralize_vector_partition_attr_values` are the single by-rowid vec0 delete primitive; all six delete sites route through it (prune_edge_projection_shadows, run_pin_and_requantize_pass, the open-path orphan sweep, both edge-supersession prunes, and the row-owned projection registry via `delete_row_owned_projection`), and `truncate_row_projections_in` gets the table-wide equivalent. Measured erasure-COMPLETE: the neutralizing UPDATE deletes the `_metadatatext<NN>` shadow row, preserves the `embedding` bytes byte-identically and preserves the other metadata columns. No-op when no `filterable` projection is declared.

LEG 3 (decision #18) — settled onto `EngineError::WriteValidation` at lib.rs:16009 (unsatisfiable `[valid_from, valid_until)` window). Rationale of record: dev/design/errors.md defines `WriteValidationError` as 'malformed typed write shape' / 'malformed before schema-sensitive payload checks run', which is exactly `validate_write`; STATUS §4 #18 prices this direction at 'one line plus tests to reverse'.

LEG 3 — the documentation defect in the locked taxonomy of record is FIXED: `EngineError::InvalidArgument` was absent from BOTH the Module-taxonomy table and the Binding-facing class matrix in dev/design/errors.md despite ~15 engine raise sites and a live InvalidArgumentError / FDB_INVALID_ARGUMENT class in both SDKs. Both tables now carry it, under a 2026-07-28 amendment note following the file's existing 2026-05-16 amendment convention.

blockers_encountered.description: LEG 4's probe was commissioned as a characterization probe that could legitimately come back clean. It did NOT: it went RED against both shipped erasure verbs. Per the brief ('If it DOES go red, then you have found the defect and TDD applies from there') I proceeded to a GREEN fix rather than committing a test that enshrines broken erasure as expected behaviour.
blockers_encountered.resolution: RED committed first (b604fc77), then the engine-side fix (980a757a). The fix is a WORKAROUND for an upstream C defect, not a cure; the durable fix is upstream and is the TC-76 recommendation. A tripwire test asserts the upstream defect is STILL PRESENT, so the workaround cannot outlive its cause silently.

blockers_encountered.description: The slice brief's site inventory for decision #18 was INCOMPLETE. It mapped one InvalidArgument site inside validate_write (lib.rs:16009). There is a SECOND, reached from the Edge branch via `reject_unrenderable_edge_epoch` (lib.rs:2159, called at lib.rs:16157-16158), which returns InvalidArgument { msg } naming the offending field and bound. A literal 'one family' collapse would have destroyed that message.
blockers_encountered.resolution: NOT collapsed, deliberately. That message is the TC-33 fix-1 contract (a codex §9 finding: an unrenderable epoch renders to `null` on the consolidation wire and silently resurrects an invalidated edge, so the caller must be told WHICH field). The settled rule is therefore stated honestly as 'the write-SHAPE boundary is one family (WriteValidation); the edge-epoch range guard is a named, tested exception', in dev/design/errors.md and CHANGELOG.md. The exception is now PINNED in tests/error_taxonomy.rs so it cannot drift in either direction. FLAGGED FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: if the board reads DoD 'one family' as absolute, this is the one item that does not meet it, and the trade is stated above.

next_step_for_orchestrator.ledger_candidate_text: LEDGER CANDIDATE (do not append — handed to the Steward, not written by me). Title: `EngineError::WriteValidation` is message-less, and 0.8.20 now spends that on a diagnostic it used to carry. Body: decision #18 (Slice 22) collapsed `validate_write`'s unsatisfiable-validity-window refusal from `InvalidArgument { msg }` onto the unit variant `WriteValidation`, which both bindings render as a FIXED, message-less string (`WriteValidationError::new_err("write validation error")` at fathomdb-py/src/lib.rs:200; `CODE_WRITE_VALIDATION` + "write validation error" + `data: Null` at fathomdb-napi/src/lib.rs:203-205). The offending `valid_from` / `valid_until` bounds are therefore no longer recoverable from the error by any caller in any language — the exact diagnostic the pre-settlement split existed to preserve, and a BREAKING behaviour change on a published surface. The same debt shows elsewhere: an `erase_source` that fails (see TC-76) surfaces a bare `StorageError` with no actionable message. The fix is a message-carrying `WriteValidation { msg }`, which is NOT a one-line change: it is cross-cutting across ~14 engine raise sites and ~44 binding raise sites and changes BOTH binding payload shapes (Python exception construction and the napi JSON envelope's `data` field), so it is properly its own slice, not a rider on Slice 22. Until it lands, the write-validation boundary trades caller diagnosability for taxonomy consistency, and one refusal (the edge-epoch range guard, TC-33 fix-1) is exempted from the collapse precisely because its message is load-bearing — which is itself the argument that the payload should exist.
deviations_stated_loudly: DEVIATION 1 (LEG 4, scope) — the leg was briefed as investigative and cheap with a written finding as the deliverable. Because the probe went RED against `erase_source` and `purge`, I also landed a fix: a new `delete_vector_partition_row` primitive routed through SIX existing by-rowid vec0 delete sites plus the table-wide truncate path. This is materially more engine change than 'a probe'. Justification: the brief said TDD applies from a red probe, and committing a green test that asserts broken erasure would have enshrined the defect. Every routed site is a mechanical substitution of an identical statement. If the orchestrator would rather ship the finding alone and defer the fix to TC-76, revert 980a757a and invert the two engine-level assertions in tc76_vec0_long_metadata_delete.rs — the RED commit b604fc77 stands on its own.

DEVIATION 2 (LEG 3, premise) — see blocker B2. The brief's statement that validate_write has exactly one InvalidArgument site is wrong; there are two. I collapsed only the one I was directed to collapse, and made the rule in errors.md and the CHANGELOG say what is actually true rather than what the DoD says literally. If the board wants an absolute 'one family', the follow-up call is whether TC-33 fix-1's field-naming message may be sacrificed — my judgement is no, and that it should wait for a message-carrying WriteValidation instead.
